Synopsis:
Opinion piece by a Nepali climate policy specialist arguing that the August 26 Nepal-Tibet glacial flash flood — which destroyed infrastructure, killed hundreds, and overwhelmed early warning systems — is a direct consequence of global inaction on climate change. The author calls for: (1) stronger cross-border early warning and mountain monitoring; (2) rapid emissions cuts by historically high-emitting nations; (3) accessible, grant-based loss & damage finance for vulnerable nations like Nepal (which contributes <0.1% of global GHG emissions). Structural critique targets the fossil fuel industry and the inequity of climate burden-sharing.
